description: Connect every row of a CSV file that can connect, each one exactly as connect_mailbox (or connect_send_only_mailbox, for a send-only row) would, up to 8 at a time, and fewer while another workspace's file waits. It answers at once, with each row queued, skipped or failed: call get_mailbox_batch until no row is queued or checking. Each queued row spends one of the workspace's 600 mailbox checks an hour, and the call itself spends one more. A file that needs more checks than are left this hour is refused whole with 429, and the call also counts toward the workspace's 10 mailbox checks a minute. A workspace runs one file at a time, so another answers 409 until it finishes. Stop a file on its way with cancel_mailbox_batch. It needs setup permission. A signed-in owner has it and can give it to an API key for the whole workspace. That key loses it if its maker stops being the owner.

content.description: The file's bytes, in base64, up to 256 KB. We read its encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16 or Windows-1252) and its separator (comma, semicolon or tab) from the bytes. Row 1 is the header; up to 50 mailboxes follow.

fileName.description: The file's name, like mailboxes.csv. It's shown back to you.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name: create_mailbox_batch
title: Connect a file of mailboxes
